  [U1] 01-before-you-get-a-dog.md · names C1: A dog lives 10 to 15 years. It needs daily exercise, company, training and veterinary care for its whole life. Before you get a dog, check that your home, your working hours and your budget fit the dog you want.
  [U2] 01-before-you-get-a-dog.md · names C1: A dog older than 4 months must be registered with the local authority and must carry a microchip.
  [U3] 03-health-and-care/01-feeding.md · names C20: Feed an adult dog twice a day and a puppy three to four times a day. Fresh water must always be available. Chocolate, grapes, onions and xylitol are poisonous to dogs.
  [U4] 03-health-and-care/02-vaccination-and-the-veterinarian.md · names C29: A puppy receives its first vaccinations at 8 weeks of age. The rabies vaccination is mandatory and must be renewed every year. Take your dog to the veterinarian for a check-up at least once a year.
  [U5] 03-health-and-care/03-grooming-and-hygiene.md · names C35: Brush your dog at least once a week; long-haired breeds need brushing every day. Trim the claws when you can hear them clicking on the floor. Wash your dog's bed and blankets once a week at 60 °C.
  [U6] 04-puppy-basics.md · names C43: A puppy is a dog younger than 6 months. Puppies should not leave their mother before 8 weeks of age.
  [U7] 05-walking-and-the-leash/02-leash-training.md · names C56: Start leash training when the puppy is 8 to 10 weeks old. Reward the dog when the leash is loose, and stop walking when the dog pulls. Never jerk the leash.
  [U8] 05-walking-and-the-leash/03-daily-walks.md · names C59: An adult dog needs at least two walks a day: 30 to 60 minutes in total for small breeds and up to 2 hours for large and working breeds. A puppy must be taken outside to relieve itself every 2 to 3 hours. Always pick up your dog's waste and put it in a waste bin.
  [U9] 06-being-a-good-lead-for-your-dog.md · names C69: Your dog looks to you for direction. Be its lead: a calm, consistent and confident leader whose signals it can trust.
  [U10] 06-being-a-good-lead-for-your-dog.md · names C69: Set clear rules (for example, whether the dog may lie on the sofa) and keep them.
  [U11] 06-being-a-good-lead-for-your-dog.md · names C69: A dog that does not see its owner as a reliable lead may become anxious or try to take control.
  [U12] 07-training-and-commands.md · names C77: Every dog should learn five basic commands: *sit*, *down*, *stay*, *come* and *leave it*. Train in short sessions of 5 to 10 minutes, several times a day, and always end with a success.
  [U13] 07-training-and-commands.md · names C77: A dog training course with a certified trainer is recommended in the first year. Dogs of breeds classified as dangerous must pass an obedience test.
  [U14] 08-leaving-your-dog-alone.md · names C84: Dogs are social animals. **Never leave an adult dog alone at home for more than 6 hours.** Puppies should not be left alone for more than 2 hours.
  [U15] 08-leaving-your-dog-alone.md · names C84: Before you leave, walk the dog, leave water and a safe chew toy, and keep your departure low-key. If your dog barks or howls while you are away, train it to be alone step by step, starting with a few minutes.

request.system:
You resolve the terms of a domain ontology after its documents were read one by one.

Each document gave its own concepts and the terms (words) that name them, so the same thing may appear as several concepts, and one word may name different things in different documents.

# Synonym groups
Give one synonym group for every concept that is named by more than one term or found in more than one document:
- concept: the alias of the concept to keep. Prefer a concept already in the ontology.
- preferred_label: the label a glossary would use, singular.
- terms: the labels of every term that names this concept.
- merge: the aliases of the other new concepts that are the same thing; they are merged into concept. Never list a concept already in the ontology here.
Only group what the text shows to be the same thing. A broader or narrower concept (a puppy is a dog) is not a synonym.

# Sense splits
When one term names different things in different units (a homonym), give a sense split:
- term: the term label.
- senses: at least two; each has the alias of the concept the term names there, a short scope_note that tells this sense apart from the others, and the aliases (U1, U2, ...) of the units where the term has this sense.

Cite concepts and units only by the aliases shown. Leave out every concept and term that needs no change.
